summary.description: Toxaphene is a yellow to amber waxy solid or gas with a turpentine-like odour, formerly used as an insecticide. It is now banned in the EU due to its environmental persistence and toxicity.
environmental_impact: Can harm lungs, nervous system, and kidneys when ingested or inhaled in large amounts
Degrades slowly and persists in the environment
Bioaccumulates in fish and wildlife and can be transported long distances through the atmosphere

top_sdg_impacts.SDG3_Good_Health_and_Wellbeing: Toxaphene exposure can affect key human organs including the lungs, nervous system, and kidneys, posing serious health risks especially in contaminated areas.
top_sdg_impacts.SDG14_Life_Below_Water: Toxaphene bioaccumulates in aquatic life, leading to toxic effects on fish and ecosystems, which disrupts marine biodiversity and food chains.
top_sdg_impacts.SDG15_Life_on_Land: Due to its persistence and bioaccumulation, toxaphene poses long-term threats to terrestrial wildlife and ecosystems, undermining biodiversity conservation efforts.
